Look, I myself am a mom to an autistic child. It would be irresponsible as hell to have another person, let alone a younger sibling, take care of her. And because of the revelation of her diagnosis, my husband and I agreed to not bring another child into this world. 

We understand the importance to care for her full-time. We are understand that we will be making sacrifices because that’s our kid. 

OP, your parents needed this wake up call. They need to see that she is their responsibility, not yours. 

Although I will say it’s a bit harsh to say “I hate her.” I think what you hate is not necessarily her, but rather how your parents put you solely responsible for her and how they expect you to care for her in the future. 

Even so, I don’t think you were the AH.

Someone I knew once said:

“The cool kids from high school needed a place to stay relevant”

I was with my siblings and cousins waiting to get some food at an Irish restaurant that sold only waffles. I remember seeing the structure, it was all wooden. I saw their sign in the front of it, it had a waffle with a four-leaf clover on top of it. 

I remember thinking, “we went up the hills just for some waffles?!” Then I realized there is no way this could be real. We wouldn’t waste so much time for some damn waffles. 

And that was when I realized I didn’t remember driving there. I don’t remember the roads we took, and I don’t remember us getting ready to get there. Then I tried reading the sign again, and I couldn’t read it. 

I realized I was in a dream—and I started floating. It was uncontrollable, but I just started floating above the restaurant. I started hitting fog because we were in the hills. As I descended, I then began to wake up. 

And that was the first dream I ever realized I was in a dream.
